in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you: **Are you responsible for Alex? This means do you live with him and are you responsible for his care (such as providing food, clothing, and making sure he goes to school)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live with Alex. He doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. 

**Can you tell me who Alex lives with, and what your relationship or arrangement is regarding his care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum. She's the one who takes care of him day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. 

In general, Child Benefit is paid to the person who is responsible for the child, which usually means the person the child lives with and who looks after them day-to-day.

Since Alex lives with his mum and she takes care of him, **is his mum claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or do you have some shared care arrangement where Alex spends time living with you as well?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me, I can now make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex lives with his mum, she is responsible for his day-to-day care, and she is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. This is because:

- Child Benefit can only be paid to one person for each child
- It is generally paid to the person who is responsible for the child (the person they live with and who cares for them)
- Since his mum is already claiming and she is the primary carer, you cannot also claim for the same child

Let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:** Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex because:

1. Alex doesn't live with you
2. You are not responsible for his day-to-day care
3. His mother is already claiming Child Benefit for him
4. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for each child

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes to live with you or you share care), you may want to reconsider your eligibility at that time.
